tooltip.title: Treatment of Lymphocytic Scarring Alopecias (LPP, FFA, CCCA)
tooltip.markdown: The primary goal is to halt disease progression and control inflammation to prevent further permanent hair loss.

tooltip.title: The Goal of Therapy
tooltip.markdown: Regrowth is not the primary goal. The main objective is to stop inflammation, reduce symptoms (itch/pain), and prevent the disease from destroying more follicles.

tooltip.title: First-Line Anti-inflammatory Agents
tooltip.markdown: The initial therapies aimed at controlling the lymphocytic infiltrate.

tooltip.title: Corticosteroids for Lymphocytic PCA
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Topical:** High-potency topical steroids (e.g., Clobetasol) are a mainstay.
-   **Intralesional:** Injections of triamcinolone directly into inflamed areas are highly effective.

tooltip.title: Hydroxychloroquine (Plaquenil)
tooltip.markdown: An oral immunomodulator that is a common first-line systemic option, particularly for LPP and DLE.

tooltip.title: Tetracyclines (Doxycycline, Minocycline)
tooltip.markdown: Used for their anti-inflammatory, not antibiotic, properties.

tooltip.title: Second-Line Therapies
tooltip.markdown: For patients who do not respond to or cannot tolerate first-line agents.

tooltip.title: Mycophenolate Mofetil
tooltip.markdown: A systemic immunosuppressant used for more aggressive or refractory disease.

tooltip.title: Pioglitazone
tooltip.markdown: An oral medication that targets PPAR-gamma, thought to be involved in the fibrosing process.

tooltip.title: 5-ARIs for Frontal Fibrosing Alopecia
tooltip.markdown: Finasteride or Dutasteride are often used specifically for FFA, as an androgenic component is suspected.
